rootCause: Memories were written and recalled without provenance. Relevance and authorization were the same test, so a high-scoring memory from any conversation was treated as current context.

findings.title: No provenance written with a memory
findings.evidence: ResponsePattern had no origin field; MemoryEngine.create wrote context: {source:'memory-engine', memoryCategory, consolidated} and nothing about conversation, session, user or time beyond createdAt.
findings.fix: MemoryEngine.create writes context.origin built by MemorySovereignty.createOrigin from the seed MemoryBridge supplies (userId, conversationId, sessionId, title, sourceType).
tests: A: a loss stated in chat A is not retrieved into chat B
D: a memory with no recorded owner is not claimed by anyone

findings.title: Recall and context assembly were unscoped; relevance was authorization
findings.evidence: brain.recall(request.prompt) received no conversation or session. Everything in the store was a candidate for every prompt.
findings.fix: Scope threaded from AIService.chat through MemoryBridge.enrich to Brain.recall → MemoryEngine.recall → PatternMemory.search, where isEligible() filters before ranking; authorize() then decides RETRIEVE / RETRIEVE_WITH_CONTEXT / DEFER / REJECT.
tests: A: one user's memory is never eligible for another user
E: an irrelevant memory from another conversation is deferred
F: simultaneous conversations do not share recalled context

findings.title: Context rendered global cognitive state without attribution
findings.evidence: buildContext printed 'Recent knowledge nodes' from brain.cognitiveState() on every turn.
findings.fix: cognitiveState(conversationId) is called with the request's conversation; nodes carry their conversation and are filtered.
tests: A: cognitive observations are rendered only in the conversation that made them

findings.title: Cognitive observations had no conversation at all (LIVE)
findings.evidence: Live run 2 (MISSION-22/live-validation.json, run before the fix): chat B's provider context matched "Recent knowledge nodes: My father died last month and I can't focus on anything." while zero memories were recalled for that turn.
findings.fix: Brain.learn passes the originating conversationId to CognitionRuntime.observe; CognitiveCore stores it on the node; CognitiveCore.state(conversationId) returns only that conversation's nodes.
tests: A: cognitive observations are rendered only in the conversation that made them

findings.title: threadContext fell back to the shared conversation window
findings.evidence: If the conversation id was not in MultiChatStore, lastTopic and recentMessages came from Brain.getConversation().context() — whichever chat spoke last.
findings.fix: With an id but no stored chat, the thread is built from the request's own messages and prompt.
tests: covered by A/F suites; exercised live (all probe turns use created conversations)

findings.title: AIService used the shared window for an unknown conversation id
findings.evidence: priorTurnsFor(...) ?? conversation.modelMessages() meant a stale id received the last chat's transcript.
findings.fix: An unknown id with chats present receives no history instead of another chat's; the shared window remains only for callers with no conversation at all.

findings.title: A high-overlap correction was reinforced instead of superseded
findings.evidence: "I prefer platinum, not rose gold" overlaps "I prefer rose gold" above the 0.6 threshold, so REINFORCE ran first and the old value stayed current.
findings.fix: The correction branch is evaluated before the high-overlap reinforce branch; the superseded value is retained in context.history and labelled as superseded.
tests: C: a correction supersedes, and the original origin never moves
E: an outdated summary is never presented as current

findings.title: Possessives were tokenised as distinct words (LIVE)
findings.evidence: Live run: "How am I handling my father's death now?" produced concepts [handling, father's, death]; the memory said "father died", so nothing matched, the authorized memory was rejected (synthesizedMemoriesUsed: 0) and the model answered "I don't have any memory of your father". A possessive is stripped before tokenisation now.
findings.fix: Strip 's before splitting, in both concepts() and sigWords().
tests: E: a possessive question still matches the stored statement

findings.title: Provenance instruction was too far away and worded against the memory (LIVE)
findings.evidence: Live run: the note sat after a 10-14k char self-state block and said historical lines are "not something the user said here"; the model read that as the user never having said it and denied a memory present in its payload.
findings.fix: The note is prepended AND appended when labelled material exists, and says the lines ARE things the user told you — in a different chat.
tests: B: the model is told how to speak about historical material

notDefects.why: It labels transcript quotes in assembled context and already worked; it cannot see structured memory records, which is why the fix belongs in the memory layer.
Already driven only by the current prompt and messages. Verified: historical grief does not change present appraisal or add support language.
Keyed by signed-in user, not by prompt. No cross-user reuse.
